title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Halloween (event week)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted historical lift: x2.65 (3 past weeks); consistent with 2023–2025 trends.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: New competitor likely draws shoppers; no prior data, but plausible demand shift; recent low sales at $4.08 suggest sensitivity.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween drives a strong historical lift (noise-adjusted x2.65), supported by three past occurrences. The price increase to $4.08 (+6%) is modest and unlikely to offset demand, especially with a new competitor across the street—this likely reduces sales. The classical model’s x2.65 is a good starting point but doesn’t account for the competitor threat. The past promotion lifts are noisy (x1.45 noise-adjusted), and this price increase is not a promotion. The recent dip (3 units at $4.08) suggests price sensitivity, but Halloween’s effect dominates. Adjust downward for the competitor, but keep the Halloween lift. No overlapping drivers. Confidence is medium due to one-time competitor event.

  median 10.3 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 24.2 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
